name: Sydney
covers: Sydney (Sydney Swans, GWS Giants, Sydney FC, Western Sydney Wanderers, Macarthur FC, NSW Waratahs; the NRL's Roosters, Rabbitohs, Bulldogs, Eels, Wests Tigers, Sea Eagles, Sharks, Panthers and Dragons), and New South Wales's State of Origin side
dialect: Australian English (Sydney and New South Wales)

words.means: The standard 425 ml glass of beer in Sydney and across New South Wales.

words.means: The smaller 285 ml glass. Melbourne and Brisbane call it a pot.

words.use: Schooner money for a schmiddy? No thanks.

words.means: Someone from Sydney. Locals use it of themselves.
words.use: Born-and-bred Sydneysider. Never missed an Origin.

words.means: A big licensed club tied to a rugby league club, with a bistro, bars and the footy on every screen. Part of suburban Sydney life.
words.use: Watch the game down the leagues club?

words.means: New South Wales's State of Origin side, in sky blue. Sydney's club rivalries go on hold when they play.
words.use: Blues need a big one in game two.

words.use: Shire born and raised. Sharks all the way.

words.means: Parramatta, the city in Sydney's west and the Eels' home.
words.use: Big crowd out at Parra tonight.

words.means: Wollongong, an hour south. The Dragons play some home games there.
words.use: Dragons are down at the Gong this week.

words.means: What many still call Sydney Olympic Park and its big stadium, where the NRL grand final is played.

words.use: Chuck your cossie in the bag, we'll hit the beach after.

words.means: A drinking fountain. Melbourne says drink tap.
words.use: Fill your bottle at the bubbler at half-time.

pronounce.why: Inner-west suburb and home of Leichhardt Oval, a Wests Tigers ground. Named after a German explorer, but nobody says it the German way.
Eastern-suburbs beach in Roosters and Rabbitohs country. The first part rhymes with 'could', not 'coo'.
Ends like 'die'. 'BON-dee' marks a tourist.
Dragons heartland in Sydney's south. Stress the first syllable; outsiders say 'koh-GAR-uh'.

lines.t: So who do you go for in the league?
lines.m: Sydney's first footy question. With nine NRL clubs in town, the answer says which part of Sydney you're from.

lines.t: Origin's the one time all of Sydney's on the same side. Go the Blues.

lines.t: Parramatta Road on a game night? Take the train.
lines.m: Sydney traffic is the standard moan before any big game.

lines.t: Southerly's come through. Should've brought a jumper.
lines.m: The cool change can turn a hot afternoon cold in minutes.

lines.t: Melbourne thinks it's the sporting capital. We've got the harbour.
lines.m: The Sydney and Melbourne rivalry, played for laughs.

avoid.why: Pot is the Melbourne and Brisbane word. In Sydney the small glass is a middy.
The beach rhymes with 'die'. Saying 'dee' marks a tourist.
Maroon is Queensland. In a Sydney pub on Origin night, wear blue or keep quiet.

habits: Sydney has nine NRL clubs, and your suburb, or your dad's, usually decides which one you go for.
Plenty of league is watched at the local leagues club or pub, with a schooner and a meal.
The NRL grand final is at Homebush, usually on the Sunday of the October long weekend.
unsure: words: 'Westie' (someone from Western Sydney) left out: some wear it with pride, others use it as a put-down, and no local source settled the tone.
words: 'Homebush' for the stadium rests on media usage (AFL.com.au, Wikipedia), not a dictionary.

name: Newcastle and the Central Coast
covers: Newcastle, the Hunter and the Central Coast (Newcastle Knights, Newcastle Jets, Central Coast Mariners)
dialect: Australian English (Newcastle, the Hunter and the Central Coast)

words.means: Someone from Newcastle. Locals say it with pride; outsiders trip over it.
words.use: Proud Novocastrian. Knights, Jets, the lot.

words.means: Newcastle. Also spelled Newie.
words.use: Back in Newy for the weekend. Knights are at home.

words.means: The Hunter Valley and the region around Newcastle: coal towns, vineyards and Maitland.
words.use: Half the Hunter comes in for a big home game.

words.means: Lake Macquarie, the big lake and the city around it, south of Newcastle.
words.use: Live down at Lake Mac, so it's twenty minutes to the game.

words.means: Charlestown, the suburb and its big shopping centre.
words.use: Meet you at Charlie, then we'll head in to the game.

words.means: Raymond Terrace, the town north of Newcastle.
words.use: He drives in from Ray Tay every home game.

words.means: Toronto, the town on Lake Macquarie. Nothing to do with Canada.
words.use: Pub in Tronno's showing the game.

words.means: The motorway between Sydney and Newcastle. It was renamed the M1 in 2013, but locals still call it the F3.
words.use: Two hours down the F3 if the traffic's kind.

words.means: Newcastle Jets against Central Coast Mariners, the region's A-League rivalry, named after the road between them.
words.use: F3 Derby Saturday. Jets or Mariners, no fence-sitting.

words.means: People from the Central Coast, and a nickname for the Mariners.
words.use: Coasties travel well. Half the away end came up the F3.

words.means: The 425 ml glass, as in Sydney. The small one is a middy.
words.use: Schooner after the game? Your shout.

Central Coast town near the Mariners' training base. It starts like 'why'.
Newcastle's famous surf beach and suburb. Said like 'merry weather', not 'MEER-weather'.

lines.t: Newcastle's a footy town. When the Knights are going well, the whole city knows it.
lines.m: The Knights are the region's one NRL club, and the city follows them closely.

lines.t: Two hours up the F3 and Sydney forgets we exist.
lines.m: The mild Newcastle grumble about being overlooked by Sydney.

lines.m: Newcastle against the Central Coast in the A-League.

lines.t: Southerly's blowing straight up the coast. Rug up for the game.
lines.m: Cold southerly changes are the weather moan all along the New South Wales coast.

avoid.why: That's how the English Newcastle says it. Here the stress is on 'New'.
Geordies come from Newcastle in England. Locals here are Novocastrians.

avoid.say: the Coast is part of Sydney
avoid.why: Coasties see themselves as their own region, with the Mariners as their team.

habits: The Knights and the Jets share one stadium in Newcastle, and a big Knights home crowd is a point of city pride.
The Central Coast has no NRL club of its own, so the Mariners are the Coast's team and league fans there follow the Knights or a Sydney club.
Fans make the trip both ways along the F3 for the F3 Derby; the trophy is made from a core of road cut from the motorway.
unsure: words: 'Maito' (Maitland) and 'Steel City' (Newcastle) left out: Maito appears only in a local headline, and no recent use of Steel City was found.
words: 'derby' is said DER-bee in Western Australia (documented); for New South Wales the same is assumed, not confirmed.

name: Canberra

words.means: Canberra's city centre. Locals rarely call it the CBD.

avoid.instead: Big crowd at Bruce this week?

Summer means cricket at Manuka Oval, which also hosts AFL games.
unsure: words: 'Gunners' (Gungahlin) left out because it clashes with Arsenal on the site; 'booner' (Canberra's bogan) left out as a put-down.
words: 'Canbrrr' (Canberra in winter) found in only one local source, so it's left out.

name: Melbourne
covers: Melbourne and Geelong (Collingwood, Carlton, Essendon, Richmond, Hawthorn, Melbourne, St Kilda, Western Bulldogs, North Melbourne, Geelong Cats, Melbourne Storm, Melbourne Victory, Melbourne City)

words.means: Someone from Melbourne. Spelled without the 'o'.

words.means: A 285 ml glass of beer, Melbourne's standard small beer. Sydney calls it a middy.

habits: Grand Final Friday is a public holiday in Victoria, with the players' parade through the city before Saturday's game at the G.
On Cup Day, the first Tuesday in November, Melbourne takes the day off: sweeps at work, then the race at 3 pm.
Fans walk to the G through Yarra Park from Richmond or Jolimont station.
With nine AFL clubs in one city, most people inherit a club from their family and stick with it for life.
unsure: lines: the MCG grand final deal to 2059 was reported in 2021; no 2026 report changing it was found.
